html:
A Mon kingdom in what is now northern Thailand, centred on the town of Lamphun in the Ping river valley, from the 7th or 8th century until 1292. The map shows it in 1000.

Chronicles say it was founded by Queen Camadevi, a princess invited from Lavo (Lopburi) to the south; the date is uncertain. Its art and inscriptions belong to the Dvaravati world of Mon Buddhist city-states. It was a centre of Theravada Buddhism, and its great shrine, Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, still stands in Lamphun.

Haripunjaya fought wars with Lavo, which fell under the Khmer in the 11th century. In the 13th century Tai peoples were building new states all around it. In 1292 Mangrai, a Tai king, besieged and took the city and made its lands the core of his new kingdom of Lan Na. He founded Chiang Mai nearby in 1296.
sum: A Mon kingdom in what is now northern Thailand, centred on the town of Lamphun in the Ping river valley, from the 7th or 8th century until 1292. The map shows it in 1000.
